mass_source: 1,200 lb (545 kg), the low end of the Model T's 540-750 kg curb-weight range (Wikipedia); early touring cars were lightest. No occupants.

steering_servo.note: Acts at the pitman; with the 4:1 planetary reduction, 60 N m there is 15 N m at the steering wheel.

suspension.note: Transverse leaf springs as linear springs on the axle joints. Front: 28 kN/m at the axle (about 70 mm static deflection under ~200 kg sprung), as a moment about the wishbone ball 0.77 m behind. Rear: 26 kN/m at the axle (about 80 mm), about the torque-tube ball 1.26 m ahead. Roll rate from a single spring whose ends sit 1.0 m (front) and 0.9 m (rear) apart: k x half-span^2 x 2, i.e. soft, as the Model T was. Damping about 0.33 of critical (interleaf friction; the Model T had no dampers). Preloads are calibrated at run time to the design ride height.

tire.note: 30 x 3 front and 30 x 3.5 rear clinchers: shared compliant contact (k 2300 s^-2, b 48 s^-1 per unit mass), round crown 40 mm half-width.

assumptions: Mass split, centre of mass (front engine), inertia, spring rates and damping are estimates.
shock_note: Stage 'shocks': each friction shock is 1.8 kg (frame arm with disc pack 1.2 kg, axle arm 0.6 kg), taken from the chassis total so the car still weighs 545 kg.
